newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH RELIEVED BUT CALL FOR FIVE NATIONS RETHINK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH RELIEVED BUT CALL FOR FIVE NATIONS RETHINK.

text.p: France are relieved the Five Nations championship is to survive in its traditional format but say its near-demise highlights the need for a revamp of the northern hemisphere's showpiece tournament.

"We have to recognise the tournament is no longer alone and unique. It must be reinforced, given an unquestioned legitimacy. We must think about other forms of competition on the global stage," said French Rugby Federation president Bernard Lapasset, reacting to the announcement of a peace deal on Thursday.

England were on the verge of being cast out of the tournament over a television revenue dispute, but a last-ditch meeting with their Welsh, Scottish and Irish counterparts saved the game's oldest international championship.

Lapasset, in an interview published in the sports daily L'Equipe on Friday, added: "I'm satisfied to see the general and sporting interest prevail over the financial aspect...and I hope the tournament will emerge stronger from this test."
But he said northern hemisphere rugby union had been close to a catastrophe and the dispute had shown the Five Nations championship was not a cast-iron event.
"We must think up another approach. We know that now there are other interests. Today the tournament is not everything," he said.

France lock Olivier Roumat said: "I wouldn't have been perturbed if England hadn't taken part again in the tournament. They would have approached the southern hemisphere nations...one day we're going to have to open up towards the rugby of the south.
"A tournament with New Zealand, South Africa, Australia, England and France would be very appealing," added Roumat who played for South African provincial champions Natal last season.
"But the Five Nations has been saved, that's a good thing. We'll play against England. For us French, it's the match of the year."

Tricolores coach Jean-Claude Skrela said: "It's very good news for northern hemisphere rugby, which will keep its most important tournament and allow it to continue to compete with the southern hemisphere.

"But which team are the English going to put out," added Skrela in jest, aware the Rugby Football Union still have to resolve their conflict with leading English clubs threatening to cause a split in the English game.
